line: Commander, on your feet! A Hive swarm just dropped out of the dark, right across the convoy's course.
They don't take prisoners and they don't bargain. Every gun we have: weapons free!
That swarm answered to Vael'Khor, the Hive Matriarch. She devours whole worlds, and now she knows our name.
Only our escape pods got clear. We came down on the nearest world we could reach, with nothing but the crew.
Every planet here orbits the Void, a black hole at the heart of the galaxy. The Hive holds most of them.
We're not alone either. Other commanders orbit the Void, and any colony can change hands.
Now we rebuild, and we grow strong enough to end Vael'Khor. I'll post directives on the Base tab. Complete them and Fleet Command will send supplies.
First things first, Commander: what should the galaxy call you? Every commander sees this name. Type it and tap Save.
Everything starts with metal. Open Structures and build your first Metal Extractor.
Extractors need power. A Solar Array keeps them running at full speed.
Crystal pays for research and better hulls. Get a refinery going.
Upgrades multiply your income. Jobs under five minutes finish for free: tap Free when it appears.
Drones, ships and research all burn gas. Get a synthesizer running.
Drone Works speeds up every construction and unlocks the Shipyard. You'll find it under Facility.
No fleet, no empire. Build the Shipyard.
Ships need engines, and engines need research. Build a Research Center under Facility.
Energy Technology is the root of the tech tree, and Combustion Drive needs it. Start it now.
Combustion Drive powers your first warships. Once it is done, the Shipyard can build Light Fighters.
Light Fighters are cheap and fast: perfect for your first raids. Queue three of them. Academy crews build them in a minute each.
The probes made it in. Open the report in Mail: it counts the defenders and tells you if your fighters would win.
Our fighters are under way. Find them on the Galaxy map and tap them: the camera follows your fleet and its control bar opens.
Every minute in transit is a minute the Hive digs in. Tap ⚡ to light the afterburners: the rest of the trip is 50% faster. This first burn is on the Academy.
Now sit back, Commander. Tap 🎥 and the camera rides in with your fighters, right into the fight.
Our fighters are closing on the garrison. Win the fight and the report lands in Mail. If they lost, send them again.
Resource fields pay out to whoever holds them. Fields already held by a rival must be fought for, so pick a free one.
Derelict pyramid stations drift all over the map. Low-level vaults are unguarded: free shards and relics.
Every battle, espionage report and message lands in Mail. Replays show you exactly why you won or lost.
Pirates hoard loot and drop rare items. This first crew is a small one: send every fighter you have.
Crystal is the rarest thing we mine, and research runs on it. Take the Crystal Refinery to Lv.5: every level digs faster. The Academy covers the cost.
Impulse Drive speeds up Colony Ships and heavier hulls, and Astrophysics needs Lv.3. Find it under Engine Research.
Better probes, and the last thing Astrophysics needs. Take Espionage Technology to Lv.4 under Advanced Research.
One more level and we can hold a second world. Every 2 levels of Astrophysics adds a planet, up to 10.
I've marked the weakest Hive world near us. Tap Espionage on its card and send your probes.
The probes are back. Open the report in Mail: it shows the defenders, their ships and the resources you could take home.
Now we know what's there. Send a fleet that outguns its garrison: the report shows exactly what you're up against.
Astrophysics Lv.2 lets us hold a second world. A Colony Ship needs Shipyard Lv.4 and Impulse Drive Lv.3.
Send the Colony Ship along with your warships to a Hive world you can beat. Win the battle and the world becomes ours: our second planet, and the first world we take back from Vael'Khor.
Our flagship is built from rare materials, and pirates hoard them. Raid another hideout: what they drop goes to the Flagship Dock. After that, the Academy clears you to build the Dock.
The Flagship Dock is where our flagship is commissioned and where its gear is forged. Find it under Structures → Facility.
Everything's ready, Commander. Commission the flagship: from now on it leads every fleet we send, gains experience and wears the gear the Dock forges.
Vael'Khor felt that. Once your Academy training is done, expect her raiders over our homeworld.
Build defenses and keep some ships at home. Chapter 2: Hold the Line.
The worlds nearer the Void are richer, and the Hive guards them harder.
Check the tech tree in Research. Heavier hulls need lasers, ion and hyperspace tech. Chapter 3: Into the Reach.
Plasma weapons and Reapers will break them. Chapter 4: Breaking the Hive.
That's the Academy done, Commander. Our flagship leads the fleet now: it earns experience in every fight, and the Flagship Dock forges its gear.
Every 2 Astrophysics levels lets us hold another world: build more Colony Ships and send them with escorts to Hive worlds we can beat. I'll keep pointing you at the next directive on your path.
And Commander: Fleet Command's supply convoy lands in 8 hours. Come back then and claim it on the Quests tab.
Commander, first blood! The garrison is broken, and Vael'Khor knows it.
Welcome back, Commander! The Academy is right where you left it, and Fleet Command sent supplies to get you moving again.

where: Economy · Upgrade the Metal Extractor to Lv.6
line: Metal is what we spend the most: every hull and every building. So metal is always our highest extractor. Take it to Lv.6.

where: Economy · Upgrade the Solar Array to Lv.7
line: Every extractor level draws more power. Whenever the Power shortage card turns red, the Solar Array comes next. Take it to Lv.7.

where: Economy · Upgrade the Crystal Refinery to Lv.6
line: Crystal comes second: research and better hulls run on it. Keep it two levels behind metal. Take the Crystal Refinery to Lv.6.

where: Economy · Upgrade the Metal Extractor to Lv.8
line: Back to metal. Metal Lv.8, Crystal Lv.6, Gas Lv.4: that is the balance strong empires run on. Take the Metal Extractor to Lv.8.

where: Economy · Upgrade the Solar Array to Lv.9
line: Power again, before the gas. The Gas Synthesizer draws the most power of all, so the Solar Array goes to Lv.9 first.

where: Economy · Upgrade the Gas Synthesizer to Lv.4
line: Gas fuels fleets and research, but we need less of it, so it stays lowest. Take it to Lv.4 and our pattern is complete: Metal 8, Crystal 6, Gas 4, with the Solar Array keeping up.

where: Economy · Upgrade your storage to Lv.2
line: Our extractors now dig faster than we can store. When a silo is full, its extractor stops. Take the Metal Silo, the Crystal Vault and the Gas Tank to Lv.2 so nothing goes to waste.
The Metal Extractor. Metal pays for almost everything we build, so keep this our highest extractor, about two levels above crystal.
The Crystal Refinery. Research and better hulls run on crystal. Keep it about two levels behind metal.
The Gas Synthesizer. Gas fuels every flight and most research. It draws the most power, so raise the Solar Array first.
The Solar Array powers every one of your extractors. When the Power shortage card turns red, upgrade this before anything else.
The Metal Silo. When it is full, the Metal Extractor stops. Raise it whenever metal sits at the cap.
The Crystal Vault. A full vault stops the refinery. Keep it ahead of your crystal income.
The Gas Tank: a full tank stops the synthesizer. Raise it as your gas income grows.
Drone Works. Every level speeds up all construction on this world. Keep it rising with your economy.
The Shipyard. Its Production tab builds ships, and its Repair tab rebuilds wrecks. Higher levels unlock heavier hulls.
The Research Center. Its Research tab opens the whole tech tree, and every level speeds research up.
The Radar Station. Its Warning tab shows enemy fleets on their way. Every level spots them five minutes sooner.
The Repair Yard. Ships wrecked in battle are towed home and rebuilt here, and it puts out fires on our worlds.
The Missile Silo stores interceptors that shoot down incoming missiles, and ballistic missiles that strike enemy defenses.
The Orbital Fortress fights for this world when it is attacked. Build it on the worlds we cannot afford to lose.
The Fusion Plant burns gas to make a lot of power. Use it when the Solar Array can't keep up, and watch your gas.
The Nanite Assembly halves every build time on this world with each level. It is the biggest speed-up we have.
The Geo-Former opens new ground: five more building fields per level. Build it when a world runs out of room.
The Coalition Depot fuels allied fleets and cuts the fuel of every flight. Its Fleets tab shows allies stationed here.
The Lunar Outpost opens building room on this world's moon. Every level adds three moon fields.
The Phalanx Array scans the space around this moon and adds a radar level for every level we build.
The Flagship Dock is where our flagship is commissioned and equipped. Its Flagship tab holds its gear.
The Warp Gate moves ships instantly between two gated worlds. It recharges after each jump.
Light Fighters are cheap, fast and the backbone of an early fleet. Build them in numbers.
Small Cargos carry plunder and supplies. Send them with your warships so a win brings the loot home.
Heavy Fighters carry real armour and shred Small Cargos. A strong step up from Light Fighters.
Large Cargos hold five Small Cargos' worth. Best for pirate raids and for moving resources between worlds.
Recyclers collect debris fields at full efficiency. Send them wherever a big battle just ended.
Pathfinders are fast long-range raiders with deep holds, deadly against Cruisers and fighters.
The Colony Ship settles a new world. Send it with warships against a Hive world we can beat, and that world becomes ours.
Cruisers are our fastest warships and the counter to any fighter swarm.
Battleships are heavy line ships: thick hulls, big guns, and deadly against Pathfinders.
Dreadnoughts hunt fleets. They punish lines of Battleships, Cruisers and Heavy Fighters.
Bombers break defenses. Send them at fortified worlds full of turrets.
Destroyers are escort killers, best against Dreadnoughts and Laser Turrets.
The Reaper is the king of the fleet. It hunts capital ships: Battleships, Bombers and Destroyers.
The Cube Destroyer is the rarest weapon in the galaxy. Only a very large fleet stands a chance against one.
Espionage Probes scout before every attack. Send more of them, or raise Espionage Technology, and the report shows more.
Mender Repair Ships patch up the fleet after every battle, and speed up the Repair Yard while parked at home.
The Guardian Heavy Cruiser is a flying shield wall that draws enemy fire away from smaller ships.
The Halo Escort Carrier launches fighter wings and protects the fleet. Deadly against fighters.
The Citadel Supercarrier is a mobile base: it commands fleets and launches squadrons.

Some building cards hold more than an upgrade. Open the Shipyard: its Repair tab rebuilds ships wrecked in battle, and its Production tab is where every ship is built. The Research Center's Research tab works the same way.
The probes made it in. Open the report in Mail and I'll walk you through it: what's stored there, what's guarding it, and whether your fighters would win.
Every battle lands in Mail with a full report. Open the report of your Hive victory and tap Watch the battle: the replay shows exactly why you won.
For stronger ships, follow the Fleet Path: every new hull needs a bigger Shipyard and new research, and its card shows the whole road with a tick for each step.
Energy Technology boosts every solar and fusion plant, and most other research needs it first.
Laser Technology arms our light weapons. Heavy Lasers and the bigger warships need it.
Ion Technology leads to Cruisers, Ion Cannons and Plasma Technology.
Hyperspace Technology adds cargo space, and unlocks the Hyperspace Drive and our heaviest warships.
Plasma Technology raises mine output a little every level, and unlocks Bombers and Plasma Turrets.
The Combustion Drive speeds up Light Fighters, cargo ships and Recyclers.
The Impulse Drive speeds up Heavy Fighters, Cruisers, Bombers and Colony Ships. Colony Ships need level 3 of it first.
The Hyperspace Drive speeds up Battleships and every capital ship. The road to the Reaper runs through it.
Espionage Technology decides how much our probes see, and how well we hide from theirs.
Computer Technology gives us one more fleet slot per level, so more fleets can fly at once.
Astrophysics lets us hold more planets: one more world for every two levels.
The Intergalactic Research Network links our labs, so every level makes research faster.
Graviton Technology is a capstone research for end-game fleets.
Weapons Technology adds ten percent damage to every ship and defense, per level.
Shielding Technology adds ten percent shield strength to every ship and defense, per level.
Armour Technology adds ten percent hull strength to every ship and defense, per level.
Cargo Logistics adds cargo space, so every raid and trade run carries home more.
Fleet Command lets our joint strikes hold more ships, and brings more allies to answer our calls.
Terraforming adds building fields on every planet we hold.
Fleet Repair Technology makes repairs faster and cheaper.
The Discovery Class Destroyer is an alliance flagship, with no limit on how many you build. Its command aura lifts the whole fleet.
This is your Finder! Everything you need outside your base is right here.
Need metal, crystal or gas? Tap Gather. Your cargo ships bring it home for free.
Pirates hide loot. Beat them and the loot is yours!
Space monsters are tough, but they drop rare treasure.
Old space stations have treasure vaults. Send ships to open them.
Cubes are giant bosses. Team up with friends to beat one.
Down here are the best picks near you right now. Tap one and go!
You can open the Finder from the map any time. Tap the question mark to see this again.
Tap the Finder button to find loot, pirates, monsters and treasure!
Your Finder has new boxes! Let me show you.
Hive Worlds are planets the Hive took over. Raid them for big piles of resources.
Events are special battles and contests, like the Cube. Come here for prizes!
The galaxy has layers. The closer to the Core, the tougher the fights and the bigger the rewards.
Commander, our flag flies over a second world! The empire now spans two worlds, and the first one we took back from the Hive.
You've built an empire, won your first battles, settled a second world and commissioned a flagship. The galaxy is yours to take.
A new fog season has begun, Commander. The charts have gone dark: only what our worlds and fleets can see is mapped. Send fleets and probes out to chart the galaxy again.
Fleet Command has registered us in the shared galaxy, Commander.
Up to ten thousand commanders orbit the Void. Any colony can change hands, so guard yours.
The Flagship Dock is where our flagship is commissioned and where its gear is forged. Find it under Structures, in Facility.

Commander, the Pyramid Overlord walks the middle layers. Beware its sigil beam, the stomp that shakes everything near it, and the surge from the beam beneath it. Four Energy Conduits feed its shield, so take them down first.
Commander, the Orbital Devourer never stops moving. Beware its snapping claws, the tentacle lash that sweeps through a fleet, and the vortex beam from its maw. Strike it with our heaviest ships.
Commander, the Void Warden guards the deep layers. Beware its void pulse, the core beam, and the satellite storm that rains lightning. Send a strong fleet, and bring our allies.
Commander, this conduit feeds the Overlord's shield. Beware its discharge, a lightning column and a shockwave when it overcharges. Destroy all four, and the Overlord takes full damage.

where: FAQ · What should I do first?
line: Build your metal, crystal and gas extractors and solar power, then follow the quests on the Quests tab. I'll always point to the next step on your path, so you're never stuck.
The Academy is your guided start. Each step teaches one system, from building your first extractor to winning your first battles, and pays a reward. Finish it and the whole galaxy opens up.

where: FAQ · Does my empire grow while I'm away?
line: Yes. Your extractors keep producing, and your building, research and shipyard queues keep running while you're offline, up to your storage limits.

where: FAQ · Am I safe as a new commander?
line: For your first three days, or until you reach 300 score, other commanders can't attack your colonies. Use that time to learn against the Hive and build your defenses.

where: FAQ · What are the resources for?
line: Metal and crystal build almost everything. Gas fuels your flights and advanced technology. Energy from solar and fusion plants keeps your extractors running at full speed.

where: FAQ · Why is my production low?
line: Check your energy. When your plants make less energy than your extractors need, every extractor slows down. Build more solar or a fusion reactor, and raise your storage so nothing overflows.
Void Shards are the rare currency. You earn them from bosses, pyramid vaults, shard mines and events, and spend them in the Void Shop on boosters, accelerators, items and VIP.

where: FAQ · How do I get more planets?
line: Research Astrophysics. Every two levels lets you hold one more world, up to ten. Then send a Colony Ship to settle or capture one. A new planet is shielded for seven days.
A battle lasts up to eight rounds. Every ship fires its own weapons; shields soak damage first, then armor and hull take the rest. You can watch every fight as a replay from Mail.

where: FAQ · Which ships should I build?
line: Every ship has a counter. Cruisers beat light fighters, dreadnoughts beat battleships, bombers beat defenses, destroyers beat dreadnoughts, and reapers beat capital ships. Mix your fleet.

where: FAQ · What happens to ships I lose?
line: Repair docks recover thirty percent of the ships you lose in any battle, and seventy percent of destroyed defenses are rebuilt. A bad fight hurts, but it won't end your empire.

where: FAQ · Why do flights cost gas?
line: Every flight burns gas, more for long trips and heavy ships. Flying slower saves a lot of fuel, and the Coalition Depot cuts the fuel for every flight.

where: FAQ · How do I spy on a planet?
line: Build espionage probes, then tap Espionage on the planet's card. More probes reveal more: the fleet, then defenses, buildings and research. Better Espionage Technology helps too.

where: FAQ · What is a joint strike?
line: A joint strike lets allies attack together. Start one on a strong target, your allies join before the timer runs out, and every fleet fights as one.
The Finder is your map search. Tap a box, like pirates, Hive worlds, mines or map events, and I'll highlight the nearest targets for you.
The galaxy has six layers around the black hole. Each layer inward has stronger enemies and richer rewards. New commanders start in the outer layers.
Pirate hideouts are full of stolen cargo. Beat the crew and your holds fill with their loot. They regroup after a raid, so come back later.
Derelict pyramid stations hold vaults of resources, shards and items. You can loot each one once a day, and from level three something still guards the halls.

where: FAQ · How do Void Shard mines work?
line: Shard mines are rare fields that pay Void Shards. A dig is slow, each mine rests for a day after your dig, and you can mine up to five shards a day.
Space monsters roam the map. Slay them for resources, shards and time accelerators that speed up your queues.
Assimilation Cubes are fortresses. One fleet rarely breaks them, so call a joint strike. They drop runes and the rarest forge materials.
Tap Cinematic view on a target's card and the camera flies around it. Drag to look around, and switch the angles at the bottom. World bosses get a full scan.

where: FAQ · What is the Battle for the Super Cube?
line: Every Friday at eighteen hundred UTC, for forty-eight hours, alliances fight to seize and hold the Super Cube. The longer your alliance holds it, the more glory and rewards you earn.
The Pyramid Overlord, the Orbital Devourer and the Void Warden return every Monday at eighteen hundred UTC. Every hit pays a bounty, and when one falls, everyone who fought it shares the spoils.

where: FAQ · What do the Energy Conduits do?
line: Four conduits feed the Pyramid Overlord's shield. While all four stand, it takes only a quarter of the damage. Destroy them first.
Galaxy War is a battle tournament every two weeks, from Monday to Wednesday UTC. Every battle point you earn counts toward milestones and rank rewards.

where: FAQ · Where are my daily rewards?
line: Open Events. Claim your daily login reward, the Online Bonus for time played, and the Level Bonus as you grow. The Daily Challenge adds more.
Allies defend your worlds, join your strikes and fight beside you for the Super Cube. Alliance bonuses make every member stronger.

where: FAQ · How do I join an alliance?
line: Open the Alliance tab, browse the list and ask to join one, or found an alliance of your own and invite your friends.
VIP raises your production and gives you free speed-ups. Earn VIP points from daily logins, events and shard purchases, and switch VIP on in the Void Shop.
Runes go into elemental rings. Fire boosts attack, water shields, earth armor, air speed, and spirit your resource output. They drop from Cube bosses and world bosses.

where: FAQ · What is a Teleport Ticket?
line: A Teleport Ticket moves one of your planets to an empty orbit. Tap an empty orbit on the map to use it.

where: FAQ · What does my commander class do?
line: The Warlord runs two extra fleets and flies warships faster on less fuel. The Industrialist carries more cargo and flies cargo ships faster. The Explorer flies frigates faster.
Your flagship leads your fleets into battle. Upgrade it in Flagship Command with forge materials from monsters, Cubes and vaults.
Yes. When you play signed in, your empire saves to the cloud as you go, so you can carry on from another device.

where: FAQ · The game feels slow. What can I do?
line: Open Settings and lower the graphics: render scale and effects. Phones run smoother on lighter settings, and the game remembers your choice.

where: FAQ · How do I turn your voice off?
line: Open Settings and switch Advisor voice off. You can turn the music and sound effects on or off there too.

where: FAQ · How do I report a problem?
line: Tap Feedback, describe what happened, and send it. Crashes and slowdowns are reported to the team automatically as well.
Commander, the world bosses have returned! The Pyramid Overlord, the Orbital Devourer and the Void Warden are loose on the map. Open the Finder to hunt them.

Commander, the Brood Matriarch is nesting in the Far Reach. Beware her hatching swarm, the acid she sprays, and the slam of her scythes. Her drones rebuild while she's left alone, so keep up the attack.

Commander, the Iron Tyrant is sailing the pirate trade lanes. Beware its broadside, the boarding claw that tears into our ships, and the mines it drops behind it. Its vault grows all week, so the later we hit it, the richer the bounty.

Commander, the Event Horizon Wyrm is coiled in the Core. Beware its gravity coil, the lens beam from its jaws, and the sweep of its tail. Strike while its glowing segments are exposed, or it shrugs off most of our fire.

Commander, the Shard Colossus has woken in the crystal fields. Beware its crystal rain, the prism beam that bounces between our ships, and the shatter when it breaks apart. It pays Void Shards in bulk.
Hatch swarm. Her egg sac squeezes and bursts, and a swarm of drones pours out to screen her.
Acid spray. She rears back and sprays acid that eats through shields.
Carapace slam. Her scythes rise and smash down in a shockwave.
Broadside. Both gun decks fire down its length, one cannon after another.
Boarding claw. The claw on its bow reaches out, grabs a ship and drags it in.
Mine wake. It drops a trail of spiked mines behind its stern.
Gravity coil. It tightens round its black hole, and the pull drags fleets in.
Lens beam. Its jaws gape and fire a lance of focused light.
Tail sweep. Its bladed tail swings round through everything near it.
Crystal rain. It raises its arms and shards hail down on the fleet.
Prism beam. A beam from its eyes splits and bounces from ship to ship.
Shatter. It bursts apart into fragments, and its heart is exposed for a moment.
Sigil beam. It rears up and fires the sigil on its face straight through a fleet.
Stomp. Its front legs slam down in a shockwave that hits everything close.
Beam surge. Its belly claws open and the beam beneath it surges.
Bite. Its claws snap shut on anything near the maw.
Tentacle lash. A whip of tentacles sweeps through the fleet.
Vortex beam. The maw gapes and fires the vortex.
Roar. Lightning crackles through everything around it.
Void pulse. Its crescents clench, then burst out in a void shockwave.
Core beam. The rings lock and the core fires.
Satellite storm. Its satellites fly wide and rain lightning.
Discharge. A lightning column and a ring shockwave.
Overcharge. Its rings spin up and the crystal overheats before it discharges.

Our alliance holds the Cube. Every minute counts. Hold the line, Commander.
Another alliance holds the Cube. Rally the fleet, Commander. We can take it back.
These are the final hours, Commander. Whoever holds the Cube at the end takes the galaxy.
There it is, the Cube, anchored over the Void. Nothing in the galaxy is bigger.
Squadrons are making their attack runs. Watch the shields flare as they hit.
Fighters are diving on the Cube in waves. Not all of them will make a second pass.
A capital ship is passing the Cube. That is where the real damage is done.
The heavy ships are trading fire with the Cube now. Hold steady.
The wreck field grows by the minute. Every hulk out there was somebody's fleet.
So much wreckage around the Void. The salvage crews will be busy for weeks.
That is a commander's flagship, leading its fleet into the fight.
A flagship is leading the charge. Commanders are fighting on the front line today.
This is your homeworld, Commander. Everything you build starts here.
These are your neighbours, the worlds orbiting closest to you. Some will be friends. Some will be targets.
This is your layer of the galaxy. Every layer further in is richer, and more dangerous.
And this is the whole galaxy. The colour around each world shows which alliance controls it.
At the very heart lies the Void, and the Cube that every alliance fights for each weekend.
Glacius has been ripped out of the Pentarch! The cold drains from its core.
Ignis breaks away! The Pentarch's flames are guttering out.
Solara is torn free, and the Pentarch's light begins to dim.
We've cut Voltaris loose! Its storm no longer answers the Pentarch.
Verdanth is wrenched away, and the Pentarch's living armour withers.
Fleets are hammering Glacius right now. Want to watch?
A battle is raging around Ignis. Take a look, Commander.
Solara is under fire as we speak. Watch it live.
Someone is taking on Voltaris right now, and the storm is fighting back!
Verdanth is under attack. Watch the battle unfold.
The Pentarch is under fire! Every commander should see this.
Glacius is shattered! One less power for the fusion.
Ignis is out, snuffed in its own smoke. Its fire will never reach the Void.
Solara has gone dark. The Pentarch will have no light to call on.
Voltaris is grounded! Its storm is spent before the Convergence.
Verdanth has withered away. Nothing green will grow inside the Pentarch.
Glacius, the ice Elemental. Every world in its path is frozen solid. Tomorrow it rides for the Void, so break it while it still stands alone.
That is Ignis, living fire. The worlds around it are burning down to cinders. Douse it now, and the fusion will burn far weaker.
Solara, the Elemental of light, is gilding the worlds around it in a blinding pillar. Dim that light before it reaches the others.
Voltaris rides a storm that never ends, and its lightning is tearing at every world nearby. Ground it before the Convergence calls.
Verdanth, the green Elemental. Whole worlds are vanishing under its growth. Cut it back now, and the Pentarch will be one power short.
They're gone. The swarm tore through every ship in the convoy.
We made it, Commander. Barely. The convoy is gone, and this world is all we have left.
This world is ours now. Give our capital a name worthy of an empire, then tap Save.
Rule one out here: never attack blind. Fleet Command just sent us four Espionage Probes. I've marked a weak Hive garrison near us: tap Espionage on its card and send the probes.
Now we know what's waiting there. Send the fighters at that garrison and show Vael'Khor we bite back.
Next goal: a second world. Astrophysics decides how many planets we can hold, and it needs Research Center Lv.3, Espionage Technology Lv.4 and Impulse Drive Lv.3. Start with the Research Center.
The pieces are in place. Start Astrophysics under Advanced Research: it charts stable orbits for settlers.
Scout before you strike. Espionage Probes slip in, count the defenders and bring back a report. They need Shipyard Lv.3 and Espionage Technology Lv.2.
Clean work. That garrison won't trouble us for a while.
Our scouts found Hive breeding grounds along the event rim, and Leviathans guard them.

where: Economy · Upgrade the Solar Array to Lv.5
line: Before we reach for a second world, our first one has to run properly. Our extractors are starved for power: Structures shows a red Power shortage card. Rule one of a strong economy: power first. Take the Solar Array to Lv.5.
A rich world draws raiders. A Radar Station spots enemy fleets on their way to us, and every level spots them sooner. Build it under Facility.
That's our homeworld in balance. Use the same order on every world we settle: power, metal, crystal, gas, storage, radar.
Our flagship is commissioned, Commander. It leads every fleet from today, and every battle it comes through makes it stronger.
That's the Academy finished. Missions will keep coming with my briefings, but from here you set the course: no more pointers, and no more free speed-ups.
Training's over, Commander. The flagship leads our fleet now, and the Dock will keep forging it better gear.
That's a Void Shark: a cruiser-sized predator with laser turrets bolted to its hide. Bring heavy hulls; it drops Exotic Tissue for the forge.
Nebula Squids hunt in packs: fast, many-armed and venomous. Bring Cruisers and armour. They drop Exotic Tissue, and sometimes Void Essence.
A Star Leviathan, Commander. Its jaws can split a battleship, so scout it first and send our heaviest fleet. It guards rare flagship materials.
A derelict pyramid station. Send an expedition to crack its vault for shards, resources and rare items. From level 3, something still guards the halls.
This Cube is a fortress, and one fleet rarely breaks it, so call a joint strike with our allies. Cubes drop Cube Fragments and Void Essence, the rarest materials in the forge.
The Super Cube is the prize of the galaxy. From Friday to Sunday, alliances fight to seize it and hold it, and every minute ours holds it earns glory and rewards for every member.
A balanced homeworld, our first victories, and room for a second world. You're ready, Commander. The missions carry on from here, with my briefings, but you lead.
Every mission done: a second world taken from the Hive, pirates raided and our flagship in command. Now the real war begins.
Every fleet we send now flies behind our flagship. Keep it fighting, and keep the Dock forging.
Good to have you back, Commander. The Academy is right where you left it, and Fleet Command sent supplies to get us moving.
Welcome back, Commander. Your missions are waiting where you left them, and there are fresh supplies from Fleet Command.
Scanning the Pyramid Overlord. Watch the sigil on its face, the stomp of its front legs, and the beam that surges beneath it.
Scanning the Orbital Devourer. Mind the snapping claws and the tentacle lash, and when its maw opens, the vortex beam.
Scanning the Void Warden. When its crescents clench, a void pulse follows. Then comes the core beam, and its satellite storm.
An Energy Conduit. When its rings spin up, expect a discharge. This is what feeds the Overlord's shield.
Commander, the Battle for the Super Cube has begun! The Cube is emerging from deep space. Rally the alliance and get ready to seize it.
The siege of the Super Cube is on! Alliances are hitting it right now. Join the battle, or watch it unfold.
Two hours left in the Cube battle. From here on, every minute we hold it counts.
The Battle for the Super Cube is over. Let's see who wears the crown.
Galaxy War has begun! For three days, every battle point we earn counts toward milestones and rank rewards.
The Pyramid Overlord is under attack! Want to watch the fight?
Someone has taken on the Orbital Devourer. The battle is live right now.
A fleet is hammering the Void Warden as we speak. Watch it live.
An Energy Conduit is under fire. Take a look, Commander.
An Energy Conduit has fallen! The Overlord's shield is weakening.
The Overlord's shield is down! Every fleet hits it at full strength now. This is our moment, Commander.
The Pyramid Overlord has fallen! If our fleets drew blood, our share of the spoils is waiting.
The Orbital Devourer is finished, Commander. Any damage we dealt earns us a cut of the spoils.
The Void Warden has gone dark for good. Check the spoils: every fleet that hurt it gets a share.
Scanning the Brood Matriarch. Her egg sac spawns a swarm, she sprays acid, and her scythes can slam down at any moment.
Scanning the Iron Tyrant: broadsides, a boarding claw, and mines in its wake. The engine at its stern runs hot, and that's our opening.
Scanning the Event Horizon Wyrm. Gravity coil, lens beam, tail sweep. Watch for the glowing segments: that's where it can be hurt.
Scanning the Shard Colossus. Crystal rain, a prism beam, and the shatter. When it breaks apart, its heart lies exposed for a moment.
The Wednesday titans have arrived! The Brood Matriarch, the Iron Tyrant, the Event Horizon Wyrm and the Shard Colossus are loose, and the Titan Hunt is on in Events.
The Brood Matriarch is under attack right now. Watch it live.
A fleet is taking on the Event Horizon Wyrm right now. Want to see it?
The Shard Colossus is under fire, Commander. Watch the crystals fly.
The Brood Matriarch is dead! Her swarm is leaderless, and everyone who fought her can claim the spoils.
The Event Horizon Wyrm is destroyed! If our fleets took part, the spoils are ours to claim.
The Shard Colossus has shattered for good, Commander. Its bounty is waiting for everyone who fought it.
This is the Pyramid Overlord, a walking pyramid fortress that hunts the middle layers beside its station. Four Energy Conduits feed its shield. Destroy them first, and it takes our full fire.
The Orbital Devourer is a world-eater that never stops moving. It roams the whole galaxy on its own path, skimming just above the worlds. Catch it where it is, and hit it with our heaviest ships.
One of four crystal pylons feeding the Overlord's shield. Bring all four down, and the Overlord takes full damage.

The Brood Matriarch, the Hive's queen. She nests in the Far Reach, and the worlds around her turn green as her infection spreads. Her swarm rebuilds whenever she's left alone, so keep the pressure on.
The Event Horizon Wyrm, a serpent of dark rings coiled around the black hole at the heart of the galaxy. Only its glowing segments can be hurt, so strike while they're exposed.
The Shard Colossus, a crystal golem grown out of the crystal fields. Badly hurt, it shatters into fragments that shield it, but it pays Void Shards in bulk.

An iron asteroid field. Its rocks are veined with glowing ore, and it's our best source of metal, and of Reinforced Alloy for the forge. Send Haulers to mine it, and keep watch: a rival can attack whoever holds the field.
A crystal comet. Its icy core bristles with crystal, so this is where we mine crystal, and Quantum Crystal for the forge. Send Haulers, and hold it until their holds are full.
A gas cloud. Our Haulers skim it for gas, the fuel every fleet burns in flight. It yields slowly, so send plenty of Haulers and keep them safe.
Scanning Glacius. Frost nova, ice lances from its orbs, and absolute zero once its rings spin up.
Voltaris on scan. Chain lightning, an ion storm that strips our shields, and the thunderclap of its crescents.
Scanning Verdanth. Thorn volleys, spore blooms, and overgrowth whenever its beam surges.
This is the Pentarch: every surviving Elemental fused into one, tearing at the black hole at the heart of the galaxy. Nothing we've faced comes close. Rally every fleet and every ally.
The Pentarch has fallen, Commander! The Void is safe again. Go and claim what we've earned.
Our alliance has seized the Super Cube! Every minute we hold it earns glory, so reinforce the garrison before the others strike back.
We've lost the Super Cube. Another alliance has taken it, so rally our allies and take it back.
Our alliance has been crowned holder of the Super Cube! Claim your rewards on the Events page.
The Elementals are gathering at the Void. The Convergence begins in ten minutes: watch it, or strike now while they're still apart.
A Clean Sweep, Commander! All five Elementals fell before the fusion, and the Convergence never formed. Claim the spoils.
The Pentarch's core has shattered! Its shards are raining across the galaxy. Gather them before they fade.
The Cube sits on the Void, and every alliance in the galaxy is closing in.
Tap any world to spy on it, attack it, send it cargo, or add it to your favourites. Where we go next is your call, Commander.
The survivors have reached the Void and fused. The Pentarch is tearing at the black hole. Everything we have, Commander: now!
A fleet has engaged the Iron Tyrant, and those broadsides are worth seeing.
We've sunk the Iron Tyrant! Its vault is open, and every fleet that fought it gets a share.

Meet the Iron Tyrant: a pirate super-dreadnought patched together from stolen hulls. It sails from hideout to hideout, and its vault fills the longer it sails. The later we strike, the richer the bounty.
Scanning Ignis now. Solar flares from its horns, magma rain, and an inferno when its core blazes.
WARNING: a celestial anomaly is tearing open beyond the Rim.
Vaelthar, the Celestial Ruin. Its wheel turns the light of dying stars. All fleets, engage!
A golden seal is forming. Our fleets are slowed inside the circle.
WARNING: CATASTROPHIC CELESTIAL ENERGY SIGNATURE DETECTED.
The wheel is aligning. Brace for impact!
We survived the blast. Now hit the wheel's stabilizers before it charges again!
Stabilizer down! The wheel is losing its balance!
Final Eclipse! The wheel is fracturing. Its core is exposed!
Vaelthar has fallen! The wheel collapses. A celestial relic drifts where it died.
WARNING: a dreadnought-class signature is dropping out of warp.
Aexion, the Warform Sovereign. Target its stern engines and shield emitters. Open fire!
WARNING: Aexion is transforming! Its hull is splitting apart!
It's standing up. That thing is a Warform!
Its holographic shield is soaking our fire. Wait for the blade, then strike!
Reactor Overdrive! Its core is exposed. Everything we have, now!
Aexion is down! Its reactor has burned out. The Warform is a wreck.
Its reactor went critical! The blast is tearing across the whole map!
Vaelthar's wheel is waking. Its stabilizers are exposed: break four of them before it charges!
Divine Judgment. The wheel is charging harder now. Keep those stabilizers down!
Final Eclipse! The wheel is fracturing and its core is exposed. Finish it!
Aexion stands in its Warform. Target the shield emitters to break its Aegis.
Reactor Overdrive! Its core is exposed. Every fleet, strike the reactor now!
Long-range sensors have found a celestial anomaly. Vaelthar arrives within three days.
A dreadnought-class signature is closing on our galaxy. Aexion arrives within three days.
Every Assimilation Cube in the galaxy is stirring. Cube Devastation begins within three days.
WARNING: a celestial anomaly is tearing open beyond the Rim. Vaelthar has arrived!
WARNING: a dreadnought-class signature is dropping out of warp. Aexion has arrived!
WARNING: CATASTROPHIC CELESTIAL ENERGY SIGNATURE DETECTED. Break the wheel's stabilizers!
The charge collapsed! Its core is exposed: strike now!
It's firing! Divine Annihilation is sweeping across the galaxy!
Aexion's reactor went critical! The blast is tearing across the whole map. Its wreckage is everywhere!
WARNING: MULTIPLE CUBE SIGNATURES ARE SYNCHRONIZING.
All one hundred Assimilation Cubes are leaving their posts. They're converging on the Void.
They're locking together, piece by piece, around the Super Cube.
The puzzle is breaking apart. No. It's rebuilding into something far bigger.
Every fleet we have is taking position. This is our Last Stand.
The Omega Cube is open to attack. Thirty-six hours. All fleets, engage!
The Last Stand has begun! Fire everything!
The fleet is gone. The Omega Cube is still standing.
It's breaking apart. The cubes are scattering home. It will return next month.
The Omega Cube is destroyed! Its cubes are scattering home, broken.
Wait. What is that? Aexion's hull is shifting...
Wait... I think it's... transforming? It IS transforming! Its whole hull is splitting apart!
Direct hit! It's staggering... its shield is breaking!
Its blade is gone! Keep up the pressure!
Its core is charging... it's going to fire! Brace yourselves!
They're back... Vaelthar has returned, and its energy readings are even stronger than before!
It's back... Aexion has returned, and it's even stronger than before. All fleets, battle stations!
Long-range sensors have found Vaelthar's signature again. It's coming back stronger, within three days.
Aexion's signature is back on our scanners, stronger than before. It arrives within three days.
Vaelthar has fallen! The wheel collapses... and a holo glyph crackles where it died.
Scanning Auricor. Beware the radiant lance, the halo burst, and judgement when its pillar of light surges.
Commander, the Elementals have torn through the Void! Gravemorn, Ignaroth, Auricor, Voltaris and Viridrax are loose in the galaxy. In a day they will fuse. Strike them down before they do.
Gravemorn joins the Convergence!
Ignaroth joins the Convergence!
Auricor joins the Convergence!
Viridrax joins the Convergence!
Gravemorn has been ripped out of the Pentarch! The dark drains from its core.
Ignaroth breaks away! The Pentarch's flames are guttering out.
Auricor is torn free, and the Pentarch's light begins to dim.
Viridrax is wrenched away, and the Pentarch's living armour withers.
Fleets are hammering Gravemorn right now. Want to watch?
A battle is raging around Ignaroth. Take a look, Commander.
Auricor is under fire as we speak. Watch it live.
Viridrax is under attack. Watch the battle unfold.
Gravemorn is shattered! One less power for the fusion.
Ignaroth is out, snuffed in its own smoke. Its fire will never reach the Void.
Auricor has gone dark. The Pentarch will have no light to call on.
Viridrax has withered away. Nothing green will grow inside the Pentarch.
Gravemorn, the void Elemental. Every world in its path is sinking into the dark. Tomorrow it rides for the Void, so break it while it still stands alone.
That is Ignaroth, living fire. The worlds around it are burning down to cinders. Douse it now, and the fusion will burn far weaker.
Auricor, the Elemental of light, is gilding the worlds around it in a blinding pillar. Dim that light before it reaches the others.
Viridrax, the green Elemental. Whole worlds are vanishing under its growth. Cut it back now, and the Pentarch will be one power short.
Scanning Gravemorn. Void nova, gravity lances from its orbs, and an event collapse once its rings spin up.
Scanning Viridrax. Thorn volleys, spore blooms, and overgrowth whenever its beam surges.
Scanning Ignaroth now. Solar flares from its horns, magma rain, and an inferno when its core blazes.
Tentacle grab!
Plasma storm!
Gravity well!
Missile volley!
I've seen a lot of battles, Commander. I have never seen anything like this.
Okay... that's new. That's very, very new.
Are you seeing this? Tell me you're seeing this too.
This is nuts. Absolutely nuts. Keep firing!
Nothing in the archives looks like this. Nothing.
I'm not going to pretend I know what that was. Just keep shooting.
Hold on. It can do that?
That shouldn't be possible. And yet, there it is.
I've run every simulation we have. Not one of them showed this.
Remind me never to say I've seen it all.
My sensors are screaming, Commander. Honestly, I don't blame them.
Wow. Just... wow. Okay, focus. Keep the pressure on!
I've been doing this a long time. This one is going in the records.
Whatever that thing is, it's rewriting the rulebook as we go.
It fights like a swordsman! A machine that size, fencing with our whole fleet!
Did it just block that? With a shield on its arm? Unbelievable.
Look at it turn. It's reading our attacks before we even make them.
The whole wheel is turning toward us... I don't even have a word for that.
Those runes are bending the space around it. I've never seen energy do that.
It's the size of a moon and it's still growing. This is insane.
Cubes are pouring off it like a storm. I've never seen the Collective do this.
That tractor beam is dragging whole squadrons in. I've never seen a pull that strong.
The entire Cube just lit up green. I've never seen it this angry.
It's swallowing the light around it. I've never seen anything do that.
Those tentacles are longer than our battleships. How is it even moving them?
Gravity readings just went off the scale. And I mean literally off it.
It's bending space around that disc. I honestly didn't think that was real.
The Pyramid is waking up... every reading I have just doubled.
It's pulling power from the whole Pyramid. I've never seen it burn this bright.
Where are all those drones coming from? It just keeps making more!
That's not a ship. That's a nest. A flying, living nest.
Look at the size of those guns. It's a fortress with engines.
It's raining missiles. I've never seen a barrage this thick.
It's coiling around that black hole like it owns it. Maybe it does.
Every segment is armoured differently. That thing was made for war.
It's held together by nothing. Just crystal, flying in formation. That's impossible.
It's rebuilding itself while we hit it. I've never seen anything heal like that.
The cold is freezing our shots in mid-flight. I didn't know ice could do that.
Its armour is actually molten. Our shells are melting before they land.
That light is so bright my scopes are going blind. Aim where you last saw it!
The lightning is jumping between our own ships. I've never seen a storm hunt like this.
It's growing back faster than we can cut it. That's not natural. Well, it is. That's the problem.
Five elements in one body. Nobody alive has seen a fusion like this.
Fire, ice, lightning, light and life, all at once. This is nuts.
All three anchors are out. Its body is exposed!
CRITICAL: DARK MATTER SINGULARITY EXPANDING. DISABLE THE GRAVITY ANCHORS.
Gravitational shockwave! It's tearing through the fleets!
Gravity readings are spiking. Space is folding in on itself out there.
It's a sphinx the size of a moon, and it's holding a black hole in its paws. I've got nothing, Commander.
It's back. Khezaroth's anomaly is opening again, and the pull is stronger than last time.
It's forming a black hole between its claws. Brace for the pulse!
It's gone. Only a relic of the sphinx is left, drifting where it fell.
Its chest armour is splitting open... that's its heart! Strike the dark-matter heart!
Its eyes just opened. Khezaroth is awake!
Its singularity is collapsing... Khezaroth is breaking apart! It's imploding!
Judgment of the Abyss. Its singularity charges every six hours. Break all three anchors before it fires!
Khezaroth, the Dark Matter Sphinx. An ancient guardian of the abyss. All fleets, engage!
Look at the size of it. Our fleets look like dust next to that thing.
Something ancient is stirring in the dark between the stars. Khezaroth wakes within three days.
Something enormous is taking shape in there. Is that... a sphinx?
The Gravity Anchor is down!
The Rune Anchor is down!
The Three Seals are awake. Three rune anchors are shielding Khezaroth: take them down to expose its body.
The Void Anchor is down!
The anchors are down and its singularity collapsed! It's stunned. Hit it now!
The gravity readings are bending again. Khezaroth is waking, within three days.
The light itself is bending around it. I've never seen gravity do that.
The starlight is bending into it... it's pulling everything in!
There are ruins in the anomaly. Ancient ones... and the runes on them are lighting up.
Those runes are older than anything in our records. Older than the galaxy maps.
WARNING: a massive gravitational anomaly is opening in the ancient sector!
It's gone. Only its glyph is left, burning where it fell.
A face the size of a moon, and it's looking right at us. I don't like this, Commander.
Five serpents down! She can't hold her gaze now!
Her eyes are opening... don't look straight into them!
Her face is cracking apart... there's a third eye in her crown! Strike the third eye!
Her gaze broke! She's blinded. Hit her now!
Her gaze is sweeping the field... our ships are turning to stone!
Her serpents are moving on their own. Every single one of them is hunting.
Her serpents are rearing and her eyes are starting to burn. Sever five of her serpent heads before her gaze charges!
Long-range scopes picked up something like a face... carved from a moon. Medusara arrives within three days.
Medusara is coming back. Keep your eyes off hers. She arrives within three days.
Medusara, the Stone Gaze. Her serpents are her eyes' shield. All fleets, engage!
She's back. Medusara's gaze is on our galaxy again, and her serpents look hungrier.
She's gone. Only her glyph is left, burning where she fell.
She's turning to stone herself... Medusara is crumbling!
The Petrifying Gaze is getting stronger. Keep cutting those serpents down!
WARNING: PETRIFYING GAZE CHARGING. SEVER HER SERPENTS, AND DON'T LOOK INTO HER EYES.
WARNING: a moon-sized stone face is rising out of a violet storm. Medusara has arrived!
We severed a serpent head!
I watched a whole squadron turn grey. Just... stone. I've never seen anything like it.
Medusara, the Petrified Star. Her serpents are her eyes' shield. All fleets, engage!

where: FAQ · Why can't I send another fleet?
line: All your fleet slots are busy. Research Computer Technology, settle more colonies, or wait for a fleet to come home. Every colony adds a slot.

where: Archives · The Keeper of the Unseen Gate · first encounter

where: Archives · The Keeper of the Unseen Gate · defeat

where: Archives · The Walking Temple · first encounter
line: The earliest records describe a pyramid that rose from the earth and walked beneath a burning sky.

where: Archives · The Walking Temple · first encounter
line: Commander... its legs are moving. The accounts were literal.
The structure is dormant. Its architecture predates everything in our database.
Perhaps the ancient empires weren't its builders. Perhaps they were trying to imitate it.

line: Commander, a massive object has emerged from deep space. Initial scans suggest biological and mechanical structures of impossible scale.

where: Archives · The Serpent That Swallowed the Moon · first encounter
line: Ancient records speak of a creature whose limbs encircled entire celestial bodies.

where: Archives · The Serpent That Swallowed the Moon · first encounter

where: Archives · The Serpent That Swallowed the Moon · defeat

where: Archives · The Plague Beneath the Stars · first encounter
line: Empire Origins records describe a black queen that brought entire kingdoms to ruin beneath a green sky.

where: Archives · The Plague Beneath the Stars · first encounter
line: Those objects surrounding her... they're eggs. Commander, they're hatching.

where: Archives · The Plague Beneath the Stars · defeat

where: Archives · The Iron Reaver · first encounter
line: Historical accounts describe a raider that appeared after the fall of several early spacefaring empires.

where: Archives · The Iron Reaver · first encounter
line: The hull is made of hundreds of separate ships. Commander, some of those designs are older than our recorded civilization.
The stolen cargo has been recovered.
But one of these ship fragments carries an insignia that should not exist in this era.

line: We are detecting movement within the black hole's accretion region.

where: Archives · The Serpent That Encircled the Sun · first encounter

where: Archives · The Serpent That Encircled the Sun · first encounter

where: Archives · The Serpent That Encircled the Sun · defeat

where: Archives · The Mountain That Remembered · first encounter

where: Archives · The Storm Tablets · first encounter
line: Those tablets described thunder that moved without clouds.

where: Archives · The Storm Tablets · first encounter
line: The ancient records called it a god. Our scanners are calling it an impossible energy structure.
Voltaris is down. The storm readings are fading.

where: Archives · The Burning Crown · first encounter
line: Commander... the artwork matches the object before us almost perfectly.
Ignaroth's fire is out.
The court astronomers drew it for a reason. I think they wanted us to recognize it.

where: Archives · The Golden Guardian · first encounter
line: The structure is emitting a highly organized pattern of light.

where: Archives · The Golden Guardian · first encounter
line: Ancient records describe a golden guardian suspended above sacred cities.

where: Archives · The Golden Guardian · first encounter
line: Those cities may not have been worshipping it. They may have been trying to communicate.
Auricor's light has gone dark.
If it was speaking to them... I wish I knew what it said.

where: Archives · The Darkness That Swallowed the Stars · first encounter
line: Commander, we're detecting a region where normal spatial measurements are becoming unreliable.

where: Archives · The Darkness That Swallowed the Stars · first encounter
line: One ancient chronicle described a purple darkness that swallowed the stars.

where: Archives · The Darkness That Swallowed the Stars · first encounter
line: I had classified that record as mythology. I am revising that assessment.

where: Archives · The Darkness That Swallowed the Stars · defeat
line: Gravemorn has collapsed in on itself.

where: Archives · The Darkness That Swallowed the Stars · defeat
line: The stars it swallowed are still there. They were simply bent out of view.

where: Archives · The Living Emerald · first encounter
line: The energy pattern resembles the green celestial symbols found throughout several ancient imperial sites.

where: Archives · The Living Emerald · first encounter
line: The ancient texts describe a living emerald presence that changed the world around it.

where: Archives · The Living Emerald · first encounter
line: Commander... the readings suggest that presence is here.
Viridrax is withering.
The cartographers marked every place it touched. We have their maps now.

where: Archives · The Five Seals of Creation · first encounter
line: Commander, five separate energy signatures are beginning to synchronize.

where: Archives · The Five Seals of Creation · first encounter
line: I've found something... a fragment from the oldest surviving imperial archive. It describes five celestial powers bound together by a ring of ancient seals.

where: Archives · The Five Seals of Creation · first encounter
line: The runes... Commander, look at the runes. They're identical. They weren't symbols of worship. They were containment instructions.

where: Archives · The Five Seals of Creation · defeat
line: The Convergence has collapsed. The surviving runes contain a message.

where: Archives · The Five Seals of Creation · defeat
line: Not a prophecy. A warning.

where: Archives · The Sleeping War Machine · first encounter
line: Commander, the unidentified vessel matches an illustration recovered from a lost imperial observatory.

where: Archives · The Sleeping War Machine · first encounter
line: The archive describes a weapon that could become a warrior. That description was considered allegorical.

where: Archives · The Sleeping War Machine · first encounter
line: It wasn't a warship. It was a weapon wearing the shape of one.

where: Archives · The Sleeping War Machine · defeat
line: Aexion's reactor is failing.

where: Archives · The Sleeping War Machine · defeat
line: But its internal design suggests it was built to fight something much larger.

where: Archives · The Dragon Behind the Sun · first encounter
line: A massive biological entity has appeared near the anomaly.

where: Archives · The Dragon Behind the Sun · first encounter
line: Ancient carvings describe a celestial dragon carrying a golden wheel upon its back.

where: Archives · The Dragon Behind the Sun · first encounter
line: Commander... the wheel is real.

where: Archives · The Dragon Behind the Sun · defeat
line: The energy has faded. I'm analyzing the damage.

where: Archives · The Dragon Behind the Sun · defeat
line: Ancient civilizations claimed this creature could erase armies with a single breath. I no longer consider that an exaggeration.

where: Archives · The Guardian of the Last Gate · first encounter
line: Commander, there's something ahead. A gravitational signature surrounding what looks like an enormous ancient monument.

where: Archives · The Guardian of the Last Gate · first encounter
line: An imperial manuscript describes a lion-shaped guardian that held a piece of darkness between its claws.

where: Archives · The Guardian of the Last Gate · first encounter
line: Commander, those are not carvings. That's a living entity.

where: Archives · The Guardian of the Last Gate · defeat
line: The Sphinx has fallen silent. The archives say it guarded a gateway.

where: Archives · The Guardian of the Last Gate · defeat
line: Commander... where is the gate?

where: Archives · The Face Beyond the Heavens · first encounter
line: Commander, long-range scans are detecting an unusual geological formation on the planet.

where: Archives · The Face Beyond the Heavens · first encounter
line: The ancient records describe a face among the stars, surrounded by serpents.

where: Archives · The Face Beyond the Heavens · first encounter
line: Those aren't mountain ranges. They're serpents.

where: Archives · The Face Beyond the Heavens · defeat
line: The planetary entity has become dormant.

where: Archives · The Face Beyond the Heavens · defeat
line: I don't know whether we defeated her, or whether she simply closed her eyes.

where: Archives · The Many-Minded Stone · first encounter
line: Commander, the navigators' guild left records of a stone of perfect angles that spoke with a thousand voices.

where: Archives · The Many-Minded Stone · first encounter
line: It's the Cube. They saw the Cube.
The Cube still stands, Commander. The navigators never said it could be destroyed.
Only held.

where: Archives · The Final Testament · first encounter
line: Commander, the archive fragments are cross-referencing on their own.

where: Archives · The Final Testament · first encounter
line: Every civilization. Every age. The same shapes, and the same warning.

where: Archives · The Final Testament · first encounter
line: We called them gods because we had no other word for what we saw.
The outer ring is accelerating. Multiple energy channels are activating.
Energy output is exceeding our instruments' calibrated range.
Commander, MOVE THE FLEET! NOW!
The energy discharge has ended. I'm analyzing the damage.
The sphere between its paws is developing an event horizon.
Destroy the gravity anchors before the singularity expands!
Massive energy accumulation detected within both ocular structures.
BREAK FORMATION! HER EYES ARE CHARGING!
Commander... the ancient accounts said her gaze turned armies to stone. We've just witnessed the technological equivalent.
Holographic shield detected. Heavy weapons active. Avoid its frontal attack arc.

where: Archives · The Keeper of the Unseen Gate · fragment
line: it stands where the stars end, and does not sleep. Its rings turn though no wind moves them. The priests say it holds the door shut. They do not say from which side...

where: Archives · The Keeper of the Unseen Gate · interpretation
line: Not a monster but a sentinel: a mass held in shape by its own field, stationed at a gravitational boundary. The 'door' in the record lines up with the region it never leaves.

where: Archives · The Keeper of the Unseen Gate · commentary
line: The archives describe it as a guardian. Every battle we've fought with it, it never came after us. It held its ground.
and the mountain of stone rose from the sand and walked, and the sky above it burned white. We built ours to remember its shape, so the gods would know we had seen...
Its geometry matches the oldest monuments to within a fraction of a degree. The records suggest the monuments were copies, not the other way round.
We always assumed the pyramids came first. What if they were sketches of something that had already stood there?

where: Archives · The Serpent That Swallowed the Moon · fragment
line: on the third night the moon was gone, and in its place a ring of arms that closed like a hand. The fishermen would not sail for a generation...

where: Archives · The Serpent That Swallowed the Moon · interpretation
line: A lunar disappearance recorded by three separate cultures in the same decade. The 'ring of arms' matches the Devourer's reach exactly.

where: Archives · The Serpent That Swallowed the Moon · commentary
line: The archives called it the Devourer. I always assumed that was a metaphor. I'm not assuming anything any more.

where: Archives · The Plague Beneath the Stars · fragment
line: a black queen under a green sky, and from her came the swarm, and the swarm did not stop at the walls. The chronicle ends here. The next page is burned...

where: Archives · The Plague Beneath the Stars · interpretation
line: The green sky is consistent with her bioluminescent egg fields seen from a planet's surface. Several kingdoms recorded the same queen, decades apart.

where: Archives · The Plague Beneath the Stars · commentary
line: Several ancient accounts describe her as one of many. That is the part of the record I like least.
it came after the colonies fell silent: a ship made of ships, wearing the hulls of everyone it had taken. Our convoy is the last. If you are reading this, change course...
A cargo log from a lost colonial convoy. Hull fragments on the Tyrant carry registry marks that match vessels the log lists as missing.
One of these ship fragments carries an insignia that should not exist in this era. Someone out there remembers the convoys.

where: Archives · The Serpent That Encircled the Sun · fragment
line: a serpent of broken rings, feeding on the light of dying stars. It does not die. It returns. Mark its return in the tables, so the ones after us are ready...

where: Archives · The Serpent That Encircled the Sun · interpretation
line: An astronomical tablet that predicts gravitational disturbances on a fixed cycle. The cycle matches the Wyrm's appearances to the week.

where: Archives · The Serpent That Encircled the Sun · commentary
line: The archive does not describe its death. It describes its return. Someone counted the years for us.

where: Archives · The Mountain That Remembered · fragment
line: we dug too deep, and the mountain woke, and its heart was purple fire. It spoke to us without a mouth. It remembered things none of us had told it...

where: Archives · The Mountain That Remembered · interpretation
line: Its central crystal is not random mineral growth: its internal structure resembles an artificial memory lattice. The miners may have heard it reading back their own thoughts.

where: Archives · The Mountain That Remembered · commentary
line: Its central crystal resembles an artificial memory lattice. If it remembered the miners... what else does it remember?
thunder that moved without clouds, and walked the sky on legs of light. First of the Five. Bound by the seal of the crescent...
Electromagnetic signatures recorded on the tablets match Voltaris's discharge pattern. The 'seal of the crescent' is one of the five runes on the Convergence ring.
The ancient records called it a god. Our scanners are calling it an impossible energy structure. I'm not sure those are different answers.
a crown of fire in the sky, and under it the kingdom burned. Second of the Five. Bound by the seal of the horn...
Court artwork of the burning crown matches Ignaroth's silhouette almost exactly, horns included.
The court painters got the horns right. They must have been looking straight at it.
a golden guardian above the sacred city, and the people sang to it every night, and every night it answered with light. Third of the Five. Bound by the seal of the ring...
Auricor emits a highly organized pattern of light. The songs may not have been worship: they may have been an attempt to answer it.

where: Archives · The Darkness That Swallowed the Stars · fragment
line: a purple darkness opened in the sky and the stars went into it, one by one, and did not come out. Fourth of the Five. Bound by the seal of the orb...

where: Archives · The Darkness That Swallowed the Stars · interpretation
line: Gravemorn bends space until normal measurements fail. From the ground, nearby stars would have appeared to vanish.
where the green star passed, the forest grew over our ships in a night. Fifth of the Five. Bound by the seal of the thorn...
Green celestial symbols appear at several ancient imperial sites. Viridrax's energy pattern matches them, and so does the overgrowth it leaves behind.
The ancient texts describe a living emerald presence that changed the world around it. The readings suggest that presence was here.

where: Archives · The Five Seals of Creation · fragment
line: five powers bound together by a ring of seals. We drew the seals on every temple so that no one would forget them. If the seals fail, the Five become One...

where: Archives · The Five Seals of Creation · interpretation
line: We believed the symbols represented the five elements. They weren't symbols of worship. They were containment instructions.

where: Archives · The Five Seals of Creation · commentary
line: Not a prophecy. A warning. Someone built that ring, and someone wanted us to know how to keep it closed.

where: Archives · The Sleeping War Machine · fragment
line: a ship that was not a ship. When it woke it stood up, and it carried a blade, and our telescope could not hold all of it in the glass...

where: Archives · The Sleeping War Machine · interpretation
line: The observatory's illustration matches Aexion's dreadnought hull. The record describes a weapon that could become a warrior. That was considered allegorical.

where: Archives · The Sleeping War Machine · commentary
line: Its internal design suggests it was built to fight something much larger. I'd like to know what.

where: Archives · The Dragon Behind the Sun · fragment
line: a dragon of the sky carrying a golden wheel upon its back. When the wheel turned, armies became light. We carved it so our children would hide when they saw it...

where: Archives · The Dragon Behind the Sun · interpretation
line: The carvings show the wheel's stabilizer spokes in the right number and position. The 'breath' that erased armies matches the Divine Annihilation beam.

where: Archives · The Guardian of the Last Gate · fragment
line: a lion that was a temple, and between its claws it held a piece of the night. It guards the last gate. Do not wake it. Do not look for the gate...

where: Archives · The Guardian of the Last Gate · interpretation
line: The 'piece of the night' is a contained singularity. The record names it a gate, and nothing we have found yet tells us where it leads.

where: Archives · The Guardian of the Last Gate · commentary
line: The archives say it guarded a gateway. We've beaten the guardian. We still haven't found the gate.

where: Archives · The Face Beyond the Heavens · fragment
line: a face among the stars, crowned with serpents, and where her eyes fell the soldiers stood still forever. The oracle wept and would not say more...

where: Archives · The Face Beyond the Heavens · interpretation
line: Her gaze is a focused energy discharge that leaves matter crystalline and inert. The armies 'turned to stone' were the technological equivalent.
a stone of perfect angles hung in the sky, and it spoke with a thousand voices that were one voice. It took our ships, and then it took our sailors, and then it took their names...
Accounts of a geometric object and a collective intelligence, centuries apart. The Collective's Cube fits every one of them, including the part about the names.
A thousand voices that were one voice. The navigators had no word for a collective. We do. It isn't any more comforting.
they will come back. Not all at once. One by one, so that you think each is the last. We have left you the shapes, the names and the seals. Learn them. We could not finish what we began...

The same symbols appear in unrelated civilizations, and the same warnings survive across thousands of years. The ancient empires were not only afraid of these entities. They were preparing for their return.
We called them gods because we had no other word for what we saw. Our ancestors weren't telling stories, Commander. They were leaving instructions.

The Concord's first deep-lane convoys called them "hull-eaters." They follow engine wakes for days and strike only when a ship turns back. The laser turrets in their hides aren't grown.
a titan-class laser platform with the heaviest hide of any monster. Send heavy hulls; Fighters barely scratch it. It drops Exotic Tissue.
Someone built those guns into them, Commander. I'd like to know who.
These serpents feed on the light of dying stars. The molten seams in their scales are star-fire they never finished digesting. Old pilots say a leviathan's wake can still burn a week later.
a capital-class plasma beast that hits harder than any other monster. Scout it, then send the heaviest fleet you have. It guards rare flagship materials.
Never fight one near a star. It gets stronger.
They hunt in packs inside gas nebulae, talking in pulses of light that our sensors read as static. Every pack has one elder that never joins the fight.
cruiser-class acid hunters that come in packs. Bring Cruisers and armour. They drop Exotic Tissue, and sometimes Void Essence.
If the pack ever goes dark at once, pull back. That's the signal.
Mantas glide the empty gulfs between layers on wings that sail on gravity itself. They're curious, and they've been seen pacing ships for hours before turning hostile without warning.
fast and evasive laser cruisers; slow guns miss them. Fighters and Lancers track them best. They drop Exotic Tissue, sometimes Void Essence.
It isn't hunting us at first. It's learning how we turn.
A queen buried in a resin nest the size of a station. The swarm grows as long as the nest is fed, and each wasp is a drone of one mind.
an acid swarm, one wasp for every level of the hive, guarding an armoured nest. Corvettes and Battleships shred the swarm; Bombers break the nest.
Leave the nest standing and the swarm comes back. Always break the nest.
Some of these are older than the moons they graze on. The crystals on their shells grow one layer a century, and miners have followed one for a whole lifetime just to harvest what it sheds.
a titan with half its damage turned aside by its shell. Bombers and plasma crack it; bring patience. It often drops Quantum Crystal.
It isn't angry, Commander. It's just very hard to move.
It carries a caged singularity that it feeds with captured ships. Its webs are bent space strung between asteroids, invisible until something is caught.
a capital-class beast with long gravity lances. Send heavy hulls, and plenty of them. It sometimes carries Void Essence.
If your fleet suddenly drifts off course, stop moving. You're in the web.
Drawn to starlight and shield light alike. Clouds of them have stripped whole defense grids bare in a single night, then drifted away glowing brighter.
ion swarms that strip shields fast, so armour matters more than shields here. Lancers run them down. They often drop Quantum Crystal.
They don't mean us harm. They just love what keeps us alive.

A horned beast of ice that rides its own comet and charges anything in its lane, ships, stations and moons alike. The herds migrate on a ring around the Core that takes three hundred years to complete.
a capital-class rammer with mass weapons that hit like a battering ram. Lead with Battleships and Bastions. It leaves Reinforced Alloy behind.
Get out of its lane or get under its horns. There's no third choice.
Kraken eggs, Commander. The clutch barely fights back, but its nest is tough. Break it for Void Essence before whatever laid it comes back.
A Ghost Whale. They only surface at night, and they slip half our shots. If you see one, hunt it now. It won't be there in the morning.
Rock Eaters. They chew through asteroids and armour alike, so send shields and hit them hard. They leave Reinforced Alloy behind.
A Celestial Serpent hatchling. Young, fast and burning hot. Bring fast ships. It often carries Void Essence.
A Petrified Sentinel. It doesn't move, but it hits like a mountain. Bring your heaviest fleet. Something old is buried in it: it drops Cube Fragments.
